query: Which method can be used for phase stability, microstructure refinement, and property optimization, and why?

generation.hypothesis: A combined thermomechanical treatment process optimized by a machine learning model can simultaneously stabilize phases, refine the microstructure, and enhance material properties in multiphase alloys.
generation.material_initial_state: A typical multiphase metallic system with coarse grains and uneven phase distribution.
generation.intervention: Application of controlled thermal cycling combined with severe plastic deformation, with processing parameters optimized via a data-driven machine learning model.
generation.conditions: Processing under varied high-temperature conditions and strain rates, implemented in a controlled thermomechanical environment.
generation.structural_mediator: A refined microstructure with homogeneous grain size and stabilized phase boundaries.
generation.mechanism: Thermal cycling promotes phase stabilization while severe plastic deformation reduces grain size, and the machine learning model systematically maps the processing–microstructure–property relationships to identify optimal conditions for concurrent optimization.
generation.predicted_outcome: A finer, more homogeneous microstructure with improved phase stability and enhanced mechanical properties (e.g., increased strength and ductility) compared to materials processed via conventional methods.
generation.baseline: Materials processed using traditional thermal treatments and mechanical processing without data-driven optimization.
generation.boundary: The method’s effectiveness is expected to be most pronounced in multiphase alloys where phase transformation and grain refinement are sensitive to processing parameters; results may vary depending on alloy composition and initial microstructure.
generation.uncertainty: The precise optimal processing parameters and the quantitative scale of improvements remain uncertain until validated by experimental trials.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of multiphase alloy samples. Process one set with the optimized thermomechanical parameters suggested by the machine learning model and the other set using conventional processing methods. Analyze and compare the phase stability, grain size distribution, and mechanical properties of both sets.
measurements: Phase composition and stability (using X-ray diffraction and transmission electron microscopy)
Grain size distribution (using electron backscatter diffraction)
Mechanical properties (via tensile strength, ductility, and creep tests)
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the optimized processing does not result in statistically significant improvements in phase stability, microstructure refinement, and mechanical properties over the conventional treatment, or if the results are inconsistent across samples, then the hypothesis is falsified.

cited_evidence.text: Abstract In the quest of new materials that can withstand severe irradiation and mechanical extremes for advanced applications ( e.g . fission & fusion reactors, space applications, etc.), design, prediction and control of advanced materials beyond current material designs become paramount. Here, through a combined experimental and simulation methodology, we design a nanocrystalline refractory high entropy alloy (RHEA) system. Compositions assessed under extreme environments and in situ electron-microscopy reveal both high thermal stability and radiation resistance. We observe grain refinement under heavy ion irradiation and resistance to dual-beam irradiation and helium implantation in the form of low defect generation and evolution, as well as no detectable grain growth. The experimental and modeling results—showing a good agreement—can be applied to design and rapidly assess other alloys subjected to extreme environmental conditions. Subject terms: Metals and alloys, Power stations

The concept of HEAs provides us an unprecedented degree of freedom in the design of advanced alloys with promising properties. For the rapid exploration of the vast compositional space and investigation of the composition and temperature effects on the microstructure, advanced HEA-design strategies and efficient tools are necessary. At present, a few advanced HEA-design strategies were reported by combining the physicochemical criteria, CALPHAD, data mining, and multi-objective optimization algorithm [21] , [22] , [35] – [37] , demonstrating that the CALPHAD method has played an important role in the design of advanced HEAs. There are two essential requirements to carry out calculations, using the CALPHAD method: computational software and database.

chosen.why: This move directly addresses the open question by implementing a method that simultaneously manipulates thermal and mechanical parameters. In materials science, combined thermomechanical treatments are a standard and practical approach to enhance phase stability, achieve microstructure refinement, and optimize material properties under well‐controlled non‐equilibrium conditions. This directly fills the niche by providing an integrated processing route that overcomes the limitations of earlier studies that often examined these aspects in isolation.

decision.trend: Early studies used conventional powder metallurgy and thermal treatments (mechanical alloying combined with spark plasma sintering, solutionizing/annealing routes) to refine grains and adjust phase distributions. Later work introduced more aggressive thermomechanical interventions (e.g., high‐pressure and high‐temperature treatment) to overcome trade‐offs between strength and ductility while promoting refined microstructures and controlled phase stabilities. Although these approaches improved individual aspects, they still involve extensive trial‐and‐error in tuning complex non‐equilibrium processing parameters.
decision.unsolved: A systematic method that can concurrently tune thermal and mechanical processing parameters to achieve robust phase stability, fine microstructure, and optimized properties remains elusive. The interdependent effects of temperature cycling, applied strain rates, and processing time require a more unified optimization strategy.
decision.lever: thermal and mechanical processing parameters via combined thermomechanical treatment
decision.why: Building on the trend toward advanced, non‐equilibrium processing methods, a data‐driven/machine learning approach can leverage existing experimental datasets to map processing–microstructure–property relationships. This would enable the systematic optimization of controlled temperature cycling and strain rate conditions to concurrently stabilize phases, refine microstructures, and enhance performance, directly addressing the identified gap.
